`budget.py` now takes an optional month: `python3 budget.py 2026-09` counts only September's transactions, and with no argument it prints the same all-time totals as before.

I ran it against your data to check:

| Envelope | No month (unchanged) | `2026-09` | `2026-08` |
|---|---|---|---|
| groceries | 174.60 | 371.55 | 403.05 |
| fuel | 22.85 | 124.75 | 78.10 |
| eating out | 45.75 | 84.25 | 111.50 |
| household | 54.61 | 101.60 | 73.01 |

- **Bad input:** anything that isn't a real `YYYY-MM` month (`2026-9`, `2026-13`) or any extra argument prints an error and exits with status 2 instead of printing a report.
- **Empty months:** a month with no transactions, like `2026-10`, shows every envelope at its full allocation.
